revision_summary: No fabricated quotes were found — all quotes check out against the transcript. However, three issues need correction on rerun: (1) MISSED MOMENT — the rep calls the customer 'Elwood' at 00:09 and 'Howard' at 06:15, two different names, never confirmed by the customer. This identity inconsistency should be surfaced as a coaching/data-integrity flag and noted as an uncertainty in the handoff_brief's stable_facts (customer's actual name is ambiguous in the record). This is a real gap a manager would want caught. (2) SCHEMA MISUSE — cherry_pick_moments[0] cites 'intros.standard' as the violated schema section, but this call is an inbound callback on an existing lead/prior touch, not a standard cold-open form-fill lead the intros.standard template is designed for. Revise to either note the ambiguity of which intro schema (if any) applies to callback scenarios, or cite a more general legitimacy principle instead of implying a template mismatch. (3) WEAK REASONING — several judgments (orphaned-flow questioning called 'halting and disorganized', interest_reason_audit dinging the rep for not probing battery motivation) apply new-solar verify-flow depth standards to what is clearly a different call type (existing-solar battery add-on/callback), without acknowledging that schema sections built for full verify calls may not directly transfer. Tighten reasoning to explicitly account for call-type mismatch before applying standard coaching expectations, consistent with how bill_anchor_audit correctly handled this contextual carve-out. The outcome_dispute reclassification to 'callback' is well-supported and should be retained as-is.
